top_band: red-brown tiled roof surface from row 2 to row 43 (light ridge band rows 3-8, sloped shingles rows 9-42, dark eave line row 43)
evidence: The building clearly shows a large foreshortened roof slope (rows 2-43) overhanging the south wall face (rows 44-78). Row 43 forms the front edge of the roof, rows 44-45 show an eave shadow on the plaster wall, and the door (rows 54-76) and window (rows 50-61) are recessed within their frames.

style.evidence: Compared to the Beodeul reference buildings, the candidate's roof tiles are large, blocky rectangles (7x3 blocks) rather than crisp individual staggered shingles with high-contrast highlights, and the roof lacks the pitched/hipped silhouette and diagonal timber bracing of the references. The window glass, shutters, lantern, and chimney use simpler geometric fills that read more cartoon-like than the dense, crispy pixel clusters of Beodeul.
